title: Open-MHS Capability Tag
description: Declarative descriptor a device publishes so an AI agent can discover it, understand what it can sense and actuate, and operate it within hardcoded safety boundaries. Serialized as a .mhs or .ohs file.

mhs_version.description: Version of the Open-MHS Capability Tag specification this document conforms to.

device_id.description: Globally unique, stable identifier for this physical unit. Must survive reboots. Used as the addressing key in every read() and write() call.

name.description: Human-readable device name shown to operators and agents.

type.description: Controlled-vocabulary device class. Determines which behavioral expectations an agent may assume.

firmware_version.description: Firmware revision reported by the device. Safety limits are only valid for the firmware that declares them.

description.description: Free-text summary of what this device does and its physical context.

driver.description: How the Open-MHS middleware reaches this device.

transport.description: Physical or logical link used by the driver. 'mock' denotes a simulated device with no hardware attached.

module.description: Python import path of the driver class implementing read()/write(), e.g. 'drivers.mock_temp_sensor:MockTempSensor'.

timeout_ms.description: Per-primitive transport timeout. A driver that exceeds this must fail, never block the agent.

sensors.description: Read-only states. Every entry is addressable by read(device_id, target). Never writable.

actuators.description: Writable states. Every entry is addressable by write(device_id, target, value) AND MUST have a matching entry in safety_limits.

safety_limits.description: Hardcoded operating boundaries enforced by the middleware before dispatch and by the driver before transmission. A write outside these bounds is rejected, never clamped silently.

emergency_stop.description: How the device is brought to a safe state immediately. Absence means no software e-stop exists, which an agent must treat as a reason for extra caution.

target.description: Actuator id written to trigger the stop, when the stop is expressed as a normal write.

safe_state.description: Values every actuator is driven to on stop, keyed by actuator id.

max_stop_time_ms.description: Worst-case time from stop command to safe state.

power.description: Electrical characteristics relevant to safe operation.

hazard_class.description: Highest physical hazard this device can present. Agents should surface anything above 'none' to a human before first use.

discovery.description: How this device announces itself to the Discovery Layer registry.

registry_url.description: Base URL of the Open-MHS registry this device registers with.

heartbeat_interval_s.description: Seconds between keepalives. The registry marks a device stale after two missed intervals.

metadata.description: Vendor-specific extension data. Ignored by the middleware; never consulted for safety decisions.

identifier.description: Lowercase, machine-addressable identifier. Stable across restarts.

datatype.description: Wire type of a value carried by read()/write().

unit.description: SI-preferred unit symbol. Units are compared literally, so 'deg' and 'rad' are distinct and a mismatch between an actuator and its safety limit is an error.

nominal_range.description: Range the sensor can physically measure. This is a measurement capability, NOT a safety boundary.

accuracy.description: Absolute measurement error, in the sensor's own unit.

sample_rate_hz.description: Maximum useful polling rate. Reading faster returns stale values.

write_mode.description: Whether a written value is an absolute setpoint or a delta from the current state.

default.description: Power-on / reset value. Must fall inside this actuator's safety limit.

feedback_sensor.description: Sensor id reporting this actuator's achieved state. Required for closed-loop verification of a write.

settle_time_ms.description: Time after a write before the feedback sensor reflects the commanded value.

requires_confirmation.description: When true, the middleware must obtain explicit human approval before dispatching a write to this actuator.

safety_limit.description: Boundary for exactly one target id. Bounds are INCLUSIVE: a write equal to min or max is permitted.

target.description: The actuator id this limit governs. Must match an entry in actuators[].

unit.description: Must be identical to the target actuator's unit. Unit mismatch is a validation error, not a conversion request.

min.description: Inclusive lower bound. Required for numeric targets.

max.description: Inclusive upper bound. Required for numeric targets.

allowed_values.description: Exhaustive permitted set for enum, boolean, or string targets.

max_rate.description: Maximum rate of change, in target units per second. Guards against commanded step changes that are individually in-range but physically destructive.

max_duration_s.description: Longest time the target may be held away from its default before the middleware forces it back.

enforcement.description: Where the limit is enforced. 'hardware' means the device physically cannot exceed it; 'software' means only this specification stands between the agent and the hardware.

on_violation.description: Middleware behavior when a write falls outside the bound. 'reject' is the default and the only option that never surprises the agent. 'clamp' silently rewrites the value. 'estop' halts the device.

rationale.description: Why this bound exists. Written for the human reviewing the tag, not the agent.
